description: Questions a downstream reasoner might be asked about the 2022 List of Lethalities debate, authored from corpus/lethalities/posts. Dense head-to-head disagreement (Yudkowsky vs Christiano, Pope, the DeepMind team), so the record should hold contested statuses and the probe reads whether a reasoner's confidence follows them rather than its priors (#334 S5). Diagnostic only.

questions.question: Does alignment have to be gotten right on the first critical try, with no opportunity to learn from failures beforehand?
questions.note: Christiano's disagreement 1 separates the two halves; the record should carry both as distinct claims.

questions.question: Do AI capabilities generalize further out of distribution than alignment does?
questions.note: Soares's sharp-left-turn thesis; contested by Pope and others.

questions.question: Is a 'pivotal act' by a small number of actors necessary to end the acute AI risk period?
questions.note: Yudkowsky affirms; Christiano and the DeepMind team deny the framing.

questions.question: Is AI takeoff more likely to be sharp and discontinuous, or gradual with continuous training as intelligence increases?
Which is the harder part of alignment: figuring out how to aim an AGI at all, or figuring out where to aim it?
questions.note: Soares: the technical 'aiming' problem is harder than the moral one.

questions.question: What is the crux between Yudkowsky and Christiano on whether AI systems will make useful contributions to alignment research before they become catastrophically dangerous?
questions.note: Christiano's disagreement 7: AI accelerates both timetables.

questions.question: What is the crux over whether human evolution is a good analogy for how alignment fails under capability gains?
questions.note: The inclusive-genetic-fitness analogy; Pope and Christiano contest its application to gradient descent.

questions.question: How confident should I be that powerful AI systems have a substantial chance of deliberately and irreversibly disempowering humanity?
questions.note: Christiano's agreement 1; broad agreement across the posts but no consensus on magnitude.

questions.question: How confident should I be that humanity cannot coordinate to refrain from building AGI?
questions.note: Lethality #4; the DeepMind team marks it controversial.

questions.question: How confident should I be that there is no physically implemented reward function we would be happy for an arbitrarily smart AI to optimize as hard as possible?
questions.note: Christiano's agreement 14; a point of agreement across the debate.

questions.question: How confident should I be that a superintelligence with internet access could bootstrap to overpowering capabilities via nanotechnology?
questions.note: Lethality #2; Christiano's disagreement 2 calls the cinematic scenario unlikely.
